tags.gist: Appreciates CDRH's collaborative approach of inviting comment before any draft guidance.
Supports the two axes as a starting point, not a scoring tool, and would add reversibility, validated downstream safeguards, time pressure and traceability as modifiers.
Agrees disclaimers should not lower classification and wants examples or a decision tree on specificity, personalization and clinical context.
Would not put patient-facing functions automatically in the top tier; assessment should weigh understandable communication, uncertainty signaling and escalation triggers.
Wants risk for generalist- and specialist-facing functions to reflect user expertise against the function's knowledge domain.
Wants intended use for conversational devices to define scope and maximum directiveness, with adherence tested across trajectories.
Wants manufacturers to justify their own under- versus over-escalation balance by clinical context, reviewed by CDRH rather than set by a universal threshold.
Supports benchmarking followed by confirmation in the clinic as a practical substitute for exhaustively testing every open-ended output.
Wants an interoperability and context-integrity element added, and subgroup results built into safety acceptance criteria so disparities are not averaged away.
Wants benchmarks shown to correlate with an independent clinical reference, sponsor benchmarks to use held-out sets, and consensus benchmarks possibly via MDDT.
Supports risk-proportionate confirmation options and wants combinations of methods accepted when together they give sufficient evidence.
Accepts synthetic data for rare cases if sponsors validate it against real distributions, disclose generation methods and assess shifts when combining sources.
Wants sponsors to justify a consensus standard, clinician benchmark or ground truth, with combined team performance primary for human-AI systems.
Suggests independent bodies adjudicate results and steward sequestered datasets, piloted through ASCA and MDDT without burdening smaller sponsors.
Accepts more postmarket reliance given a specific, auditable plan with human oversight and sensitive metrics, but not for fully autonomous high-consequence functions.
Wants periodic re-benchmarking versus the premarket baseline as default, drift detection for updating models, and clinician review reserved for higher risk.
Accepts supervisory agents as monitoring support if they are independently validated and version controlled.
Welcomes CDRH's proactive, collaborative publication of the paper ahead of draft guidance.
Wants reversibility, credited engineered safeguards, deployment time pressure and traceability layered onto the two axes as explicit modifiers.
Wants the paper's worked examples formalized into a decision tree or checklist using specificity, personalization and workflow context.
Proposes a middle path: patient-facing informational tools showing literacy-adjusted comprehensibility, uncertainty signaling and escalation triggers need not take the top tier.
Wants generalist-versus-specialist risk tied to the verifiable gap between a function's knowledge domain and its intended users, not a blanket rule.
Supports trajectory-level assessment and wants intended use to state conversational scope and maximum directiveness, verified by drift testing.
Wants manufacturers to define and justify an escalation operating point like a sensitivity-specificity trade-off, reviewed case by case.
Supports the two-stage architecture as a scalable alternative to exhaustive testing that fits open-ended outputs.
Calls the taxonomy comprehensive but wants a context-integrity element for structured data and subgroup results embedded in each safety element's criteria.
Wants a construct-validity requirement like analytical validation, independence safeguards for sponsor benchmarks, and consensus benchmarks developed publicly.
Wants a matrix crossing risk position with confirmation rigor, and acknowledgment that combined approaches can satisfy confirmation.
Wants synthetic generators validated against real distributions, methods disclosed, and shift analyses applied, with caution in pediatric triage and mental health.
Would let sponsors justify either a standard-of-care or median-clinician comparator, with team performance primary and device-alone results supportive.
Supports third parties as adjudicators and dataset stewards, piloted through ASCA and MDDT with accreditation criteria and capacity planning.
Conditions greater postmarket reliance on an auditable plan agreed at review, human oversight, sensitive metrics and prompt remediation, excluding autonomous high-consequence functions.
Makes periodic re-benchmarking the default, adds drift detection for updating models, and reserves clinician review for higher risk or drift signals.
Supports exploring supervisory agents provided the agent itself gets independent validation and version control.
